name: Alain Voge Cornas Les Vieilles Fontaines 2012
text:
## Alain Voge Cornas Les Vieilles Fontaines 2012

**The story.** Domaine Alain Voge is in [Cornas](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Domaine+Alain+Voge,+Cornas,+France&t=k), a small village in the [Ardèche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ard%C3%A8che) just north of [Valence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valence,_Dr%C3%B4me), on the [Rhône](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rh%C3%B4ne) in the [northern Rhône](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rh%C3%B4ne_wine) wine region. Alain Voge's great-grandfather Henri brought the family there in the early 20th century, when vines were just one part of a mixed farm. Alain, born in 1939, started working on the estate in 1961. When his father Louis died in 1965, he took charge alongside his mother ([Decanter](https://www.decanter.com/obituaries/alain-voge-dies-cornas-rhone-443632/)).

Over the next decades Voge became one of the small group who built Cornas's international name. He worked with a merchant to sell the wine in bottle rather than in bulk, and fought to protect the vineyards from the town's spread. He replanted the family's vines in the heart of Cornas (giving "Les Vieilles Vignes" in the 1970s) and helped bring the neighbouring white-wine appellation of [Saint-Péray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-P%C3%A9ray_AOC) back to life. Decanter's Rhône expert Matt Walls said that leading one appellation is impressive, but leading two is rare ([Decanter](https://www.decanter.com/obituaries/alain-voge-dies-cornas-rhone-443632/)).

In 2004 Albéric Mazoyer, previously a winemaker at [Michel Chapoutier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chapoutier), joined as a partner and manager. [Organic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organic_farming) and then [biodynamic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodynamic_agriculture) certification followed; the [estate](https://www.alain-voge.com/en/cornas/les-vieilles-fontaines) says its vines and wine were certified organic from the 2016 vintage. Mazoyer handed over to Lionel Fraisse in October 2018. Alain Voge died in September 2020, aged 81 ([Decanter](https://www.decanter.com/obituaries/alain-voge-dies-cornas-rhone-443632/)).

**The vineyard: Les Vieilles Fontaines.** The name means "the old springs". In the locality called La Fontaine there is a spring that once supplied water to the house of a noble Cornas family. Voge first made this wine there in 1988, from the estate's oldest [Syrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrah): about 0.9 hectares of vines now around 80 years old, on [granite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granite). It is made only in exceptional years; the estate lists 2009, 2010, 2012 and 2015 among the recent ones ([the estate's page](https://www.alain-voge.com/en/cornas/les-vieilles-fontaines)). Cornas is 100% Syrah by law ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornas_AOC)). You can look over the steep Cornas slopes from above [here](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Cornas,+Ard%C3%A8che,+France&t=k).

**How it's made.** The [estate's current sheet](https://www.alain-voge.com/en/cornas/les-vieilles-fontaines) gives: Syrah vines trained as free-standing bushes on single stakes ([gobelet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vine_training)); hand-picked; partly destemmed, with about 30% whole bunches; wild-yeast fermentation and several weeks of maceration in steel vats, with daily punching-down and pumping-over; then 24 months in 228-litre Burgundy-size [barrels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_%28wine%29), 15 to 20% of them new. Only about 2,400 bottles are made, and the estate gives it 25 years of ageing potential. (Details may have varied a little in older vintages.)

**Cornas itself.** The appellation is small: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornas_AOC) gives about 90 hectares, and the [estate](https://www.alain-voge.com/en/cornas/les-vieilles-fontaines) says 145 today. By comparison, some single Bordeaux châteaux are bigger than the whole of Cornas. The vines grow on steep, east- to south-east-facing slopes of granite and sandy, rocky soil. Cornas is sheltered from the [mistral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mistral_%28wind%29) and is often the first northern Rhône appellation to harvest. Traditional Cornas was known as a tough, tannic wine needing 6 to 7 years before it was approachable ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornas_AOC)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [northern Rhône vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/northern-rhone) says 2012 went well for the Rhône, against the trend in the rest of Europe. Potential alcohol was lower than usual, so some growers even added sugar during fermentation ([chaptalisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaptalization)), and acidity was also below normal, while the tannins were firmer than in 2011. She adds a warning that, with age, 2012 has proved an inconsistent vintage, so the producer matters a great deal. Voge chose to make Vieilles Fontaines in 2012, which it does only in years it judges exceptional, and the critics agreed (below). Down the road at A. Clape, [Wine Spectator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wine_Spectator)'s James Molesworth found yields so low in 2012 that one of their wines came to only 100 cases ([his Cornas report](https://www.winespectator.com/blogs/show/id/49331)).

**What the critics say for 2012.** The earlier note on this wine said no critic score could be found. I found three:
- **[Wine Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wine_Advocate): 97** ([as listed by the US merchant SommPicks](https://www.sommpicks.com/products/2012-alain-voge-cornas-les-vieilles-fontaines-750ml-2-eu); the reviewer isn't named there). Tasting it a year after a first look, the reviewer called it one of the top wines of the vintage: black raspberry and cassis with chocolate, violets, licorice and a touch of minerality; big, full-bodied and voluptuous, with great purity. He expected it to seem more classic Cornas after a few years and to live 20 years or more.
- **[Vinous](https://vinous.com): 95** ([also listed by SommPicks](https://www.sommpicks.com/products/2012-alain-voge-cornas-les-vieilles-fontaines-750ml-2-eu)). Bright purple, intensely perfumed with dark berry preserves, cherry-cola, Indian spices and potpourri; fresh and pure, deeply concentrated blackcurrant, and a long smoky finish with "sneaky" tannins.
- **[Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson): 17.5/20** ([Richard Hemming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Hemming), from barrel in 2014, [listed by SommPicks](https://www.sommpicks.com/products/2012-alain-voge-cornas-les-vieilles-fontaines-750ml-2-eu)). He noted the 80-year-old vines, freshly sawn oak and succulent black fruit, and praised the wine for being subtle and graceful rather than over-extracted or heavy, as many top cuvées are. On her stricter scale, that is a strong score.
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 95.3** (from your CellarTracker list). Unusually, drinkers rate it about as highly as the critics.

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is fourteen years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2022 to 2032, and the [Wine Advocate](https://www.sommpicks.com/products/2012-alain-voge-cornas-les-vieilles-fontaines-750ml-2-eu) expected 20 years or more overall. It should be in a lovely place now, the oak absorbed and the dark fruit, violets and smoky, savoury notes of Cornas to the fore, with years still ahead. No hurry, but no reason to wait either.

**Serving.** [Decant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decantation) about an hour ahead, both to wake it up and to leave any sediment behind, and serve at 16 to 17°C in a large glass. If it seems tight at first, give it more air; Syrah of this structure often opens over the evening.

**Food.** Northern Rhône Syrah loves game and peppery, savoury dishes. My picks: [venison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venison) or roast lamb, duck breast with a [black-pepper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_pepper) sauce, a grilled [rib-eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rib_eye_steak), or a mushroom and black-olive [tapenade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tapenade) dish. Hard cheeses work too. I'd avoid delicate fish and sweet, sticky sauces.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the three stores on this site lists it. The US merchant [SommPicks](https://www.sommpicks.com/products/2012-alain-voge-cornas-les-vieilles-fontaines-750ml-2-eu) offers the 2012 at about US$95, sold in cases of six. At the domaine, the [current 2023 vintage](https://www.alain-voge.com/en/cornas/les-vieilles-fontaines) sells for €93, limited to three bottles per customer. For a 97-point Cornas from 80-year-old vines, that is fair value.

**From the history books**
- **"Burnt earth".** The name Cornas comes from the language of the [Celts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celts) and means "burnt earth", fitting for its sun-baked slopes. Wine from Cornas is mentioned in writing as early as 885 AD. It is said (though hard to prove) that [Louis XV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_XV) and [Cardinal Richelieu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Richelieu) both admired it ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornas_AOC)).
- **A late starter in bottle.** Cornas became an official [appellation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appellation_d'origine_contr%C3%B4l%C3%A9e) in 1938, but local growers only began bottling their own wine around 1950 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornas_AOC)). [Pierre-Auguste Clape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Auguste+Clape+Cornas&go=Go), who died in 2018 aged 93, began bottling his own Cornas in the 1950s, and Alain Voge belonged to the same pioneering generation that made Cornas known abroad ([Decanter](https://www.decanter.com/obituaries/alain-voge-dies-cornas-rhone-443632/)).
- **Saving the slopes.** Voge spent the 1970s and 1980s replanting and regenerating old Cornas vineyard sites, and became a leading voice in protecting the vineyards from the spread of housing ([Decanter](https://www.decanter.com/obituaries/alain-voge-dies-cornas-rhone-443632/)).
- **A first for Cornas.** In December 2012 [Robert Parker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Parker_%28wine_critic%29) gave the 2010 Vieilles Fontaines 100 points, the first perfect score for any Cornas. He called it one of the few perfect Cornas he had ever tasted ([the estate's page](https://www.alain-voge.com/en/cornas/les-vieilles-fontaines)).
- **Saint-Péray reborn.** Voge also pioneered barrel-fermented still white wines in neighbouring [Saint-Péray](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Saint-P%C3%A9ray,+Ard%C3%A8che,+France&t=k) in the 1980s and is credited with revitalising that appellation ([Decanter](https://www.decanter.com/obituaries/alain-voge-dies-cornas-rhone-443632/)). The estate's Saint-Péray range includes one called "Les Bulles d'Alain" ("Alain's bubbles").

**Curious details**
- **A chef's pairing.** For this wine the [estate](https://www.alain-voge.com/en/cornas/les-vieilles-fontaines) suggests venison in [sake lees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sake_kasu), a dish created by chef [Anne-Sophie Pic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne-Sophie_Pic) at [her restaurant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maison_Pic) in nearby [Valence](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Maison+Pic,+Valence,+France&t=k).
- **Tiny production.** About 2,400 bottles a year, from less than one hectare, and only in great years ([the estate's page](https://www.alain-voge.com/en/cornas/les-vieilles-fontaines)).
- **Smaller than a château.** The whole Cornas appellation makes less wine than some single Bordeaux estates ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornas_AOC)).
- **The spring is real.** The "fontaine" of the name is an actual spring in the La Fontaine locality, which once fed a noble family's house ([the estate's page](https://www.alain-voge.com/en/cornas/les-vieilles-fontaines)).
